extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, primacy agencies, and drinking-water public-notification preparers/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required language for public notification under the National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (Part 141): maps specific violations, contaminants, and situations to notification tiers, cites applicable regulatory sections, and provides standard health-effects language to include in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier classification for violations (Tier 1, 2, 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations and situations are assigned to Tier 1, Tier 2, or Tier 3 public notice categories as indicated in the Appendix table; primacy agencies may require more stringent tiers under §141.202(a) and §141.203(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier selection drives the required timing, content, and delivery methods of public notices; specific violations throughout the table indicate the applicable tier number (1, 2, or 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations of NPDWR include MCL, MRDL, TT, monitoring, and testing procedure violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Violations of National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (NPDWR)' includes violations of MCL, MRDL, treatment technique (TT), monitoring, and testing procedure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notices are required not only for exceedances of MCL/MRDL/TT but also for failures to monitor or follow testing procedures (see Note 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy agency discretion to require more stringent tier
rubrics_metrics.description: Primacy agencies may, at their option, require a more stringent public notice tier (e.g., Tier 1 instead of Tier 2) for specific violations and situations listed in this Appendix, as authorized under §141.202(a) and §141.203(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must follow primacy agency determinations about tiering which may be stricter than the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total coliform (standard health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: See footnote. Standard language: 'Coliforms are bacteria that are naturally present in the environment and are used as an indicator that other, potentially-harmful, bacteria may be present. Coliforms were found in more samples than allowed and this was a warning of potential problems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided text in public notification when total coliform violations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecal coliform / E. coli (standard health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: Zero. Standard language: 'Fecal coliforms and E. coli are bacteria whose presence indicates that the water may be contaminated with human or animal wastes. Microbes in these wastes can cause short-term effects, such as diarrhea, cramps, nausea, headaches, or other symptoms. They may pose a special health risk for infants, young children, some of the elderly, and people with severely compromised immune systems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full required text for notices involving fecal coliform or E. coli detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecal indicators (GWR): E. coli, enterococci, coliphage (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero/None/None; MCL/TT as applicable. Standard language: 'Fecal indicators are microbes whose presence indicates that the water may be contaminated with human or animal wastes. Microbes in these wastes can cause short-term health effects, such as diarrhea, cramps, nausea, headaches, or other symptoms. They may pose a special health risk for infants, young children, some of the elderly, and people with severely compromised immune systems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the provided language for Ground Water Rule fecal indicator detections and GWR TT violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground Water Rule (GWR) TT violations (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: None. MCL/TT: TT. Standard language: 'Inadequately treated or inadequately protected water may contain disease-causing organisms. These organisms can cause symptoms such as diarrhea, nausea, cramps, and associated headaches.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this health-effects language when GWR treatment technique violations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart Y Coliform Assessment and/or Corrective Action Violations (required mandatory sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCL: TT. Standard language explains coliforms as indicators and that an assessment/corrective action is required. Required sentences: 'We failed to conduct the required assessment.' and 'We failed to correct all identified sanitary defects that were found during the assessment(s).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this violation applies the system MUST include the applicable mandatory sentences in its notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart Y E. coli Assessment and/or Corrective Action Violations (required mandatory sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCL: TT. Standard language indicates E. coli signifies contamination and risk (greater risk for infants, elderly, immunocompromised). Required sentences: 'We failed to conduct the required assessment.' and 'We failed to correct all identified sanitary defects that were found during the assessment that we conducted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the mandatory sentences when Subpart Y E. coli assessment/corrective action violations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli (notice triggering conditions and standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. E. coli is in compliance unless one of listed conditions occurs (e.g., E. coli-positive repeat sample, total coliform-positive repeat after E. coli-positive routine sample, failure to take required repeat samples, failure to test for E. coli when required). Standard language describes E. coli health effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed triggering conditions and include the E. coli health-effects language when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart Y Seasonal System TT Violations (notice language instructions)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCL: TT. Guidance: When violation includes failure to monitor for total coliforms or E. coli prior to serving water, use mandatory language in §141.205(d)(2); for other failures, use elements in §141.205(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select specific language elements based on which actions were missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity (MCL) (standard health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: None. MCL: 1 NTU / 5 NTU (as applicable). Standard language: 'Turbidity has no health effects. However, turbidity can interfere with disinfection and provide a medium for microbial growth. Turbidity may indicate the presence of disease-causing organisms. These organisms include bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause symptoms such as nausea, cramps, diarrhea and associated headaches.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when turbidity MCLs are exceeded; separate entries exist for SWTR TT and IESWTR/LT1ESWTR turbidity TTs with same health-effects framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity (SWTR TT) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: None. MCL/TT: TT. Standard language same as turbidity MCL above; applies to Surface Water Treatment Rule treatment technique violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specified language in notices for SWTR treatment technique violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity (IESWTR TT and LT1ESWTR TT) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: None. TT. Standard language same as turbidity entries above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when Interim Enhanced SWTR or Long Term 1 ESWTR turbidity TTs occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giardia lamblia (SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL/TT: TT. Standard language: 'Inadequately treated water may contain disease-causing organisms. These organisms include bacteria, viruses, and parasites which can cause symptoms such as nausea, cramps, diarrhea, and associated headaches.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this language for Giardia-related surface-water treatment rule violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viruses (SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR violations requiring the standard disease-causing organism language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard organism language when viruses are implicated under these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterotrophic plate count (HPC) bacteria (SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed with TT and the standard organism health-effects language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specified organism language for HPC violations under surface water rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legionella (SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed with TT and standard organism language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use organism health-effects language for Legionella-related TTs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium (IESWTR/FBRR/LT1ESWTR) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Included under IESWTR/FBRR/LT1ESWTR with TT and standard organism language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply organism language for Cryptosporidium violations; Note 22: Failure to collect three or more samples for Cryptosporidium analysis is a Tier 2 violation requiring special notice as specified in §141.211; all other monitoring/testing procedure violations are Tier 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antimony (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.006 mg/L. MCL: 0.006 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing antimony well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience increases in blood cholesterol and decreases in blood sugar.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this language for antimony MCL exceedances in public notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arsenic (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0. MCL: 0.010 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing arsenic in excess of the MCL over many years could experience skin damage or problems with their circulatory system, and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arsenic MCL citations have effective dates noted in endnotes; use the provided language and correct citation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asbestos (fibers >10 µm) (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 7 MFL. MCL: 7 MFL. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing asbestos in excess of the MCL over many years may have an increased risk of developing benign intestinal polyps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include asbestos-specific health-effects sentence for asbestos MCL exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barium (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 2 mg/L. MCL: 2 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing barium in excess of the MCL over many years could experience an increase in their blood pressure.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for barium MCL exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beryllium (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.004 mg/L. MCL: 0.004 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing beryllium well in excess of the MCL over many years could develop intestinal lesions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for beryllium MCL exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadmium (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.005 mg/L. MCL: 0.005 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing cadmium in excess of the MCL over many years could experience kidney damage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in notices for cadmium exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chromium (total) (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.1 mg/L. MCL: 0.1 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who use water containing chromium well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience allergic dermatitis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for chromium MCL exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyanide (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.2 mg/L. MCL: 0.2 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing cyanide well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience nerve damage or problems with their thyroid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cyanide health-effects wording in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluoride (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 4.0 mg/L. MCL: 4.0 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing fluoride in excess of the MCL over many years could get bone disease, including pain and tenderness of the bones. Fluoride in drinking water at half the MCL or more may cause mottling of children's teeth...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the full fluoride health-effects sentence; separate Appendix item for SMCL fluoride exceedance notification (other situations section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mercury (inorganic) (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.002 mg/L. MCL: 0.002 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing inorganic mercury well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience kidney damage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for inorganic mercury exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrate (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 10 mg/L. MCL: 10 mg/L. Standard language: 'Infants below the age of six months who drink water containing nitrate in excess of the MCL could become seriously ill and, if untreated, may die. Symptoms include shortness of breath and blue baby syndrome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 12: Failure to take a confirmation sample within 24 hours for nitrate or nitrite after an initial sample exceeds the MCL is a Tier 1 violation. Other monitoring violations for nitrate are Tier 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrite (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 1 mg/L. MCL: 1 mg/L. Standard language: 'Infants below the age of six months who drink water containing nitrite in excess of the MCL could become seriously ill and, if untreated, may die. Symptoms include shortness of breath and blue baby syndrome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above for nitrate; confirmation-sample requirements affect tiering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Nitrate and Nitrite (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 10 mg/L. MCL: 10 mg/L. Standard language: 'Infants below the age of six months who drink water containing nitrate and nitrite in excess of the MCL could become seriously ill... blue baby syndrome.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include total-nitrate-and-nitrite language where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selenium (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.05 mg/L. MCL: 0.05 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing selenium in excess of the MCL over many years could experience hair or fingernail losses, numbness in fingers or toes, or problems with their circulation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for selenium exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thallium (IOCs) (MCL and health-effects language)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.0005 mg/L. MCL: 0.002 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing thallium in excess of the MCL over many years could experience hair loss, changes in their blood, or problems with their kidneys, intestines, or liver.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include thallium-specific language for notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead (Lead and Copper Rule) (standard language and action level)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: zero. Action level (lead): 0.015 mg/L (action-level exceedances are TT). Standard language: 'There is no safe level of lead in drinking water. Exposure to lead in drinking water can cause serious health effects in all age groups, especially pregnant people, infants... Decreases in IQ and attention span... Adults have increased risks of heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or nervous system problems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full lead health-effects language for lead action level exceedances; the Lead and Copper Rule contains specific TT and sampling/response requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copper (Lead and Copper Rule) (standard language and action level)
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 1.3 mg/L (action level). Standard language: 'Copper is an essential nutrient, but some people who drink water containing copper in excess of the action level over a relatively short amount of time could experience gastrointestinal distress... Over many years could suffer liver or kidney damage. People with Wilson's Disease should consult their personal doctor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include copper-specific wording for notices where the action level is exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic Organic Chemicals (SOCs) standard health-effects entries (general instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SOC listed (e.g., 2,4-D; 2,4,5-TP; Alachlor; Atrazine; Benzo(a)pyrene; Carbofuran; Chlordane; etc.) includes an MCL and a standard sentence describing likely long-term health effects (examples: kidney, liver, reproductive issues, increased cancer risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each SOC MCL exceedance use the contaminant-specific health-effects sentence provided in Appendix B; examples follow for individual SOCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2,4-D (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.07 mg/L. MCL: 0.07 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing the weed killer 2,4-D well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience problems with their kidneys, liver, or adrenal glands.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this text for 2,4-D MCL exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2,4,5-TP (Silvex) (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.05 mg/L. MCL: 0.05 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing silvex in excess of the MCL over many years could experience liver problems.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for Silvex exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alachlor (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 0.002 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing alachlor in excess of the MCL over many years could have problems with their eyes, liver, kidneys, or spleen, or experience anemia, and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include for alachlor exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atrazine (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.003 mg/L. MCL: 0.003 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing atrazine well in excess of the MCL over many years could experience problems with their cardiovascular system or reproductive difficulties.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for atrazine exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benzo(a)pyrene (PAHs) (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 0.0002 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing benzo(a)pyrene in excess of the MCL over many years may experience reproductive difficulties and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include for benzo(a)pyrene exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dioxin (2,3,7,8-TCDD) (SOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 3 × 10^-8 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing dioxin in excess of the MCL in excess over many years could experience reproductive difficulties and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for dioxin exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS and PFAS constituents (Hazard Index PFAS, HFPO-DA, PFHxS, PFNA, PFOA, PFOS) (standard language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hazard Index MCL: 1 (unitless). Individual PFAS MCLs (HFPO-DA, PFHxS, PFNA, PFOA, PFOS) listed with specific mg/L values (e.g., HFPO-DA 0.00001 mg/L). Standard language: PFAS can persist in the body and lead to increased risks (liver, immune, thyroid effects; developmental effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 23: Systems that violate the Hazard Index MCL and one or more individual MCLs based on the same contaminants may issue one notification to satisfy public-notification requirements for multiple violations pursuant to §141.203. Use contaminant-specific language for each PFAS as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volatile Organic Chemicals (VOCs) standard health-effects entries (general instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each VOC listed (e.g., Benzene; Carbon tetrachloride; Chlorobenzene; dichloroethylenes; Dichloromethane; 1,2-Dichloropropane; Ethylbenzene; Styrene; Tetrachloroethylene; Toluene; Vinyl chloride; Xylenes) includes an MCL and a standard sentence describing likely long-term health effects such as cancer or organ damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each VOC MCL exceedance use the contaminant-specific health-effects sentence provided in Appendix B; examples follow for individual VOCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benzene (VOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 0.005 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing benzene in excess of the MCL over many years could experience anemia or a decrease in blood platelets, and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for benzene exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vinyl chloride (VOC) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 0.002 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing vinyl chloride in excess of the MCL over many years may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in notices for vinyl chloride exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radioactive contaminants health-effects language (beta/photon, alpha, combined radium, uranium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beta/photon emitters: MCLG Zero; MCL 4 mrem/yr. Alpha emitters: MCLG Zero; MCL 17 pCi/L. Combined radium (226 & 228): MCLG Zero; MCL 5 pCi/L. Uranium: MCLG 16 µg/L; MCL 30 µg/L. Standard language describes increased cancer risk and other health effects for long-term exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided radioactive contaminant language for notices; uranium health-effects language specifically mentions cancer and kidney toxicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection Byproducts (DBPs), Byproduct Precursors, Disinfectant Residuals (general instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA sets standards for controlling disinfectants and DBPs, including TTHMs, HAA5, bromate, chlorite, and MRDLs for disinfectants (chlorine, chloramine, chlorine dioxide). Each listed DBP has an MCL or MRDL and a standard health-effects sentence to use in notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply contaminant-specific language (TTHMs MCL 0.080 mg/L, HAA5 0.060 mg/L, bromate 0.010 mg/L, chlorite 1.0 mg/L, etc.). Additional procedural guidance exists for chlorine dioxide monitoring and follow-up sampling (see Notes 15 and 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Trihalomethanes (TTHMs) (DBP) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCL: 0.080 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing trihalomethanes in excess of the MCL over many years may experience problems with their liver, kidneys, or central nervous system, and may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TTHM language for TTHM exceedances; note timing/effectivity clauses in endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Haloacetic Acids (HAA5) (DBP) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCL: 0.060 mg/L. Standard language: 'Some people who drink water containing haloacetic acids in excess of the MCL over many years may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use HAA-specific language for HAA exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bromate (DBP) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: Zero. MCL: 0.010 mg/L. 'Some people who drink water containing bromate in excess of the MCL over many years may have an increased risk of getting cancer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for bromate exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorite (DBP) health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: MCLG: 0.08 mg/L. MCL: 1.0 mg/L. 'Some infants and young children who drink water containing chlorite in excess of the MCL could experience nervous system effects. Similar effects may occur in fetuses of pregnant women who drink water containing chlorite in excess of the MCL. Some people may experience anemia.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include chlorite-specific wording in notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine and chloramine (MRDL) language
rubrics_metrics.description: Chlorine (MRDL) and Chloramine (MRDL) entries reference MRDL language and health-effect references; specific citations are provided (e.g., §141.65(a), §141.132).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MRDL notification requirements and include appropriate health-effects language where MRDLs are exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine dioxide (MRDL) monitoring and tiering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Chlorine dioxide MRDL exceedances at the entrance to distribution system require follow-up sampling: If any 2 consecutive daily samples at entrance to distribution system only are above MRDL, citations include §141.65(a) and §141.133(c)(3); if distribution system samples the next day are also above MRDL, Tier 1 notification is required. Failure to monitor the next day is a Tier 2 violation (Note 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to take required distribution system samples after an entrance exceedance triggers Tier 1; failure to monitor next day is Tier 2. Use the specified regulatory citations and notice language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of DBP precursors—TOC (Treatment Technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of total organic carbon (TOC) as a treatment technique (TT) is listed (see §141.135(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When this TT is violated, include appropriate DBP precursor/TOC language and citations (§141.132(a), (d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarking and disinfection profiling (monitoring/reporting guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bench marking and disinfection profiling are referenced (citations §141.172 and §141.530-141.544).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are monitoring and operational practices that, if required or violated, have associated notice/reporting responsibilities per the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of monitoring plan (DBP-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of a monitoring plan is cited (§141.132(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems required to develop monitoring plans must follow notice and reporting requirements associated with monitoring plan implementation and violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Treatment Techniques: Acrylamide and Epichlorohydrin (TT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acrylamide and Epichlorohydrin are listed as Treatment Techniques under §141.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When TT requirements for these contaminants are violated, include appropriate TT notice language per §141.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregulated contaminant monitoring (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some systems must monitor for specified unregulated contaminants in §141.40; Appendix indicates unregulated contaminants and nickel monitoring requirements and cites §141.23(c),(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data may require public notification (see Other Situations Requiring Public Notification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notification for operation under a variance or exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Operation under a variance or exemption triggers public-notification requirements (references to §§1415 and 1416 of the SDWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must reflect schedule and compliance milestones as required by §§1415/1416 and, for small systems, items specified in 40 CFR 142.307.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notification for violation of conditions of a variance or exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating conditions of a granted variance/exemption requires public notification (citations to §§1415/1416 and 40 CFR 142.307).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must include items and schedule milestones specified in 40 CFR 142.307 for small systems as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other situations requiring public notification (category list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other situations requiring public notice include: Fluoride SMCL exceedance; Exceedance of nitrate MCL for non-community systems as allowed by primacy agency; Availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data; Waterborne disease outbreak; Other waterborne emergency; Source water sample positive for GWR fecal indicators; Other situations as determined by the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each situation may have specific notice language and tiering; e.g., waterborne disease outbreak and other waterborne emergencies typically require Tier 1 notification (Note 20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluoride secondary maximum contaminant level (SMCL) exceedance (other situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluoride SMCL exceedance is listed as an 'Other Situation Requiring Public Notification' with citation §143.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate SMCL notice language when fluoride secondary MCLs are exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceedance of nitrate MCL for non-community systems (primacy-agency allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-community systems may have nitrate MCL exceedances as allowed by primacy agency; citation §141.11(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow primacy-agency determinations and include nitrate health-effects language as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data (notice requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must notify the public about the availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring data (citation §141.40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible information describing the monitoring and results as required by regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waterborne disease outbreak (notification requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Waterborne disease outbreaks require public notification (citation §141.2, §141.71(c)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These situations usually require Tier 1 notification and the urgent language specified for acute health threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other waterborne emergency (Tier 1 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other waterborne emergencies requiring Tier 1 public notice include situations with potential for serious adverse health effects due to short-term exposure (e.g., treatment failures, natural disasters, chemical spills, unexpected pathogen loading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Tier 1 required timing and delivery methods for these emergencies; Note 20 provides examples and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water sample positive for GWR fecal indicators (notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: A source water sample positive for GWR fecal indicators (E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage) triggers notification obligations (citation §141.402(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include GWR fecal-indicator language and follow GWR notice protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other situations as determined by primacy agency (discretionary notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primacy agencies may place other situations in any tier they believe appropriate based on threat to public health (Note 21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must follow primacy-agency instructions regarding tiering and notice content for discretionary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to test for fecal coliform or E. coli after positive repeat sample (tiering rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to test for fecal coliform or E. coli is a Tier 1 violation if testing is not done after any repeat sample tests positive for coliform. All other total coliform monitoring and testing procedure violations are Tier 3 (Note 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring/testing failures can change the tier and thereby change required notice urgency and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity MCL average over two consecutive days (primacy consultation / automatic elevation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that violate turbidity MCL of 5 NTU based on an average over two consecutive days must consult with the primacy agency within 24 hours after learning of the violation. The primacy agency may elevate to Tier 1; if system cannot contact the agency within 24 hours, the violation is automatically elevated to Tier 1 (Note 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation timing and inability to contact the primacy agency affect tier assignment and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single exceedance of a maximum turbidity limit (consultation / elevation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems with treatment technique violations involving a single exceedance of a maximum turbidity limit under SWTR, IESWTR, or LT1ESWTR must consult the primacy agency within 24 hours; the agency may elevate to Tier 1; if unable to contact the primacy agency in 24 hours, the violation is automatically elevated to Tier 1 (Note 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt consultation is required and affects tiering and notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to collect three or more Cryptosporidium samples (tiering rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to collect three or more samples for Cryptosporidium analysis is a Tier 2 violation requiring special notice as specified in §141.211. All other monitoring and testing procedure violations are Tier 3 (Note 22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection failures can produce Tier 2 notices with specific content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Index PFAS combined-notice allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that violate the Hazard Index MCL and one or more individual MCLs based on the same contaminants may issue one notification to satisfy public-notification requirements for multiple violations pursuant to §141.203 (Note 23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may consolidate notices for overlapping PFAS exceedances per §141.203 to avoid duplicate notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and phased implementation notes (endnotes guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix endnotes specify effective dates and phased compliance schedules for various rules and contaminants (e.g., certain IESWTR requirements effective Jan 1, 2002 for systems serving ≥10,000; arsenic MCL citations effective Jan 23, 2006; uranium MCL Tier dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices and citations must use the correct regulatory citation and effective date relevant to the system's type and service population per the endnotes.
